title: Gate 1 assessment (smooth posterior + v2 observation, reduced authoritative sweep)
combined_rule: Gate 1 passes iff the rate-axis gate passes AND boundary_f1 > 0.
runner_verdict_note: The companion runner stamps incomplete-sweep because only the frozen arm ran (the joint validity control was not part of this Gate-1 protocol). That is expected and is not the Gate-1 decision.

rate_distortion_shape.note: Rate spans 0.001->0.69 (~600x) for only a 0.045 distortion improvement (1.4997->1.4551). Steering itself drops distortion from the 2.4239 unsteered baseline to ~1.50, but time-varying high-information codes add almost nothing. This is the OPPOSITE of the ETA near-vertical gap prediction.

interpretation: The smooth posterior reparameterization fixed the rate axis: spearman moved from -0.657 (legacy, non-monotone rebound at alpha=1.0) to a perfect -1.0, and seed variance collapsed. The instrument is now clean and the monotonicity confound is removed.

The v2 observation protocol removed the leakage (source_text and completed-objectives) that previously made segmentation trivially unnecessary; the audit showed v2 forces intra-route ambiguity in 74/88 routes.

With both confounds removed, the controller still never switches (max boundary_f1 = 0, max hard_switch_frequency = 0; mean switch probability peaks at 0.456, under the frozen 0.55 threshold) and the rate-distortion curve is near-horizontal rather than near-vertical.

This is a clean, un-confounded negative: at Qwen2.5-0.5B and this scale the ETA signature (steep gap + subgoal-aligned switching) does not appear. The learned control collapses to a near-constant steering direction, matching the degenerate 'switch once' baseline the paper warns about.
next_step: Do NOT proceed to Stage 2 continued pretraining on the strength of temporal abstraction. The rate-axis mechanism is now healthy, so the remaining question is scale/substrate capacity, not the posterior artifact. Any further ETA claim must first show a near-vertical gap and boundary_f1 > 0 on a larger substrate before spending pretraining compute.
